Adversarial review — crates/lumen-model, lumen-session, lumen-pattern, lumen-analysis, lumen-store

Ledger Audit

Six independent review passes — bug hunt, security, spec-drift verification, architecture, and simplification — run against this session's 22 commits. The short version: the test suite is green, and the pricing engine is wrong for almost every real session.

5
Blocker
9
High
11
Medium
0
Security vulns
60
Files scanned
96/96
Tests passing

The headline

Every dollar figure is suspect

PricingTable::rate_for matches model names by exact string equality. No adapter normalizes a raw provider string (claude-opus-4-20250514, gemini-2.0-flash-001) to the short seeded key (claude-opus, gemini-2.0-flash) before calling it. Every one of those misses falls through the "unrecognized model" guard and gets billed at Claude 3.5 Sonnet's rate — silently, with no warning or log line.

This was verified by direct execution, not inference: rate_for("claude-3-5-haiku-20241022", ...), rate_for("claude-opus-4-20250514", ...), rate_for("gpt-4o-2024-08-06", ...), and rate_for("gemini-2.0-flash-001", ...) all return Sonnet's $3.00 / $3.75 / $0.30 / $15.00 per-M rates. Claude 3.5 Sonnet is the only model priced correctly today, and only by coincidence — it's the fallback target.

A second, independent bug compounds it: any Codex session that reports a service_tier (the fixture itself carries one) prices the entire session at $0.00, because the pricing table has no tiered rows and the tier filter simply finds nothing to match.

Blocker

5 findings

Wrong output with no visible failure. Each of these passes the current test suite.

Blockercrates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs:118–135
No model-string normalization anywhere in the workspace

Confirmed by canon:drift-checker against every provider criterion: 9 of 20 pricing acceptance criteria are drifted, all from this one root cause. claude.rs passes the raw message.model field straight through; agy.rs, codex.rs, and opencode.rs never reassign model_family from its hardcoded default at all.

Trigger & fix

Trigger: ingest any real session from any of the four adapters. Real model strings carry date suffixes or provider prefixes the seed table's short keys don't.

Fix: add a normalization step in rate_for (or immediately before calling it) that strips known version suffixes to the canonical key — the spec's own PricingTable api_surface entry already promises this behavior, it was just never implemented.

Blockercrates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs:134 · codex.rs:148
Any Codex service_tier zeroes the entire session's cost

PricingTable::seed() pushes every row with tier: None. When a Codex payload sets tier: Some("Standard"), the tier-equality filter matches zero rows for all four rate kinds, and unwrap_or(0.0) silently returns $0.00. The shipped Codex test fixture carries service_tier: "Standard" — a real session, priced at zero, and the test never asserts the cost.

Fix

Fall back to the tier: None row when no tiered row matches, and consider making rate_for return Option<f64> so an unpriceable combination is visible to the caller instead of collapsing to zero.

Blockerspecs/SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE.json · crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/
The store spec certifies five repository types that don't exist

ToolCallRepository, RollupRepository, CommandEventRepository, SnapshotRepository, and TokenUsageRepository all appear in the spec's api_surface with full method signatures. Only findings.rs, queue.rs, and session.rs exist. The spec text explicitly claims tool_counts_by_session/error_counts_by_session replaced a hardcoded BTreeMap::new() — session.rs:160–161 still hardcodes it. This is the exact "spec certifies fictional code" failure the earlier research pass was meant to eliminate, reintroduced in the same commit meant to fix it.

Blockercrates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs:65
Unrecognized session files silently parse as fake, empty, successful reports

detect_orchestrator(sample).unwrap_or(OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode). When fingerprinting fails — any Kimi, GenericOtel, or malformed file — the CLI guesses ClaudeCode. ClaudeCodeAdapter::parse_stream cannot fail on wrong-schema input: every field read defaults quietly, so it returns Ok(CanonicalTranscript) with zero turns, session_id: "unknown", and a full $0.0000 economics table. This is the workspace's one real production binary — lumen scan counts each such file as a discovered session, and lumen audit exits 0 with a clean-looking report on a file it never actually read.

Blockercrates/lumen-model — CanonicalTurn · trajectory_dag.rs:45 · pr_link.rs:71
A structural type gap, not a local bug — two accumulators built on a state the system never reaches

CanonicalTurn can hold both tool_calls and tool_results, but no adapter ever populates both on the same turn — a call and its result always land on separate turns. Two accumulators correlate the two within one turn and therefore always produce a constant: TrajectoryDagAccumulator's had_error is false for every node in every real session, and PrLinkAccumulator's linked_via_vcs_tool is always 0. A test at test_accumulators.rs:1447 asserts the always-false behavior as if it were intended.

Why this is architectural, not a patch

Patching these two call sites individually won't stop the next accumulator from making the same reasonable-looking assumption against the same type. The fix belongs at the CanonicalTranscript model level — a cross-turn call_id correlation pass, run once by an adapter or a shared post-processing step, not re-derived per accumulator.

High

9 findings
Highfingerprint.rs · codex.rs:18 · opencode.rs:17–21
detect_orchestrator and matches_fingerprint disagree — for three of four adapters

detect_orchestrator is an ordered if-chain (Claude → AGY → Codex → OpenCode), so a later branch implicitly means "no earlier marker matched." Every adapter's own matches_fingerprint is a bare substring test with no such precedence. A sample carrying both a Claude and a Codex marker: detect_orchestrator says ClaudeCode, CodexAdapter::matches_fingerprint says yes too. Confirmed empirically for both Codex and OpenCode; Claude's own matches_fingerprint additionally still runs the old, untightened OR-condition instead of this session's sessionId + parentUuid rule.

Highcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs:84–104, 145, 156–157
The explicit-null guard only checks top-level fields — the fields it names live nested

Three of the nine fields the null-rejection guard was written to protect — model, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens — are read from message.model and message.usage.*, never the entry's top level. An explicit null there is silently coerced to 0 or the hardcoded default instead of being rejected as malformed. The regression test covers exactly one of the nine named fields.

Highcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/opencode.rs:82
A dollar amount silently shadows the input-token count

usage_obj.get("accumulated_cost").or_else(|| usage_obj.get("input_tokens")) — when both keys are present, the cost value wins the lookup. as_u64() on that float returns None, unwrap_or(0) silently records zero input tokens, and the turn is still accepted because output_tokens alone satisfies the non-empty guard.

Highcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/agy.rs:45
AgyAdapter's model is permanently hardcoded to a Claude model name

model_family is set once, to "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", and never reassigned anywhere in the file. Antigravity is a Gemini-lineage orchestrator; there isn't even a matching Gemini seed row it could hit if the real model string were extracted. Every AGY session is priced as Claude Sonnet, forever, silently.

Highclaude.rs:69, codex.rs:66 · agy.rs:64,189 · opencode.rs:61,226
Parse-failure records are half-built and half-missing

byte_offset is hardcoded to the literal 0 in every ParseFailureRecord claude.rs or codex.rs construct — the field exists, nothing ever computes it. Worse: AgyAdapter and OpenCodeAdapter silently discard malformed lines (Err(_) => continue) and hardcode parse_failures: SmallVec::new() on the returned transcript — a corrupted Antigravity or OpenCode session reports as perfectly clean.

Highcrates/lumen-analysis/src/engine.rs:121–125
Subagent reports silently overwrite each other on a session_id collision

by_subagent is keyed by subagent.session_id — but claude.rs only replaces the default "unknown" session id when a top-level sessionId field appears, which real subagent JSONL commonly lacks. Two subagents with no explicit id both key to "unknown"; the second insert silently drops the first subagent's entire report. The field built specifically to disambiguate siblings — subagent_role ("worker-a", "worker-b") — sits right there on the struct and is never used as the key.

Highcrates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs:5
A boundary-truncated UTF-8 byte collapses the whole fingerprint sample

std::str::from_utf8(sample_bytes).unwrap_or("") reads the first 2048 bytes of a file. If any multi-byte character — an emoji or accented character in a real user prompt, routine in real transcripts — straddles that boundary, the conversion fails and all 2047 valid preceding bytes are discarded, not just the broken tail. A well-formed file becomes unrecognizable purely by chance of where the boundary lands.

Highcrates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs:131 · pricing.rs (TokenRateKind)
Reasoning tokens are tracked but structurally can never be priced

TokenRateKind has exactly four variants — Input, CacheWrite, CacheRead, Output — no Reasoning. Codex's adapter parses a real reasoning_output_tokens value and assigns it to the returned struct after TokenEconomics::calculate has already summed total_cost_usd. The field reaches the struct; it never reaches the pricing math. This isn't a bug in one call site — no adapter, ever, can price reasoning tokens under the current rate-kind enum.

Highcrates/lumen-store/src/repositories/session.rs · migrations.rs:71
Token economics is a write-only field in the store — and its own table is dead

upsert_session never binds input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens/reasoning_output_tokens/per_model as INSERT params, even though real, non-zero values exist upstream. get_session can only hardcode them back to zero on read — there's no column to read from. Separately, the token_usage table (6 columns, its own migration) has zero INSERT or SELECT anywhere in the codebase. Currently inert only because lumen-cli never calls into lumen-store at all — see Architecture, below.

Medium

11 findings
Mediumcrates/lumen-pattern/src/lib.rs:139–149
Grounding score contradicts its own documented convention

compute_grounding_score's path-checking arm covers FileRead/FileEdit but not FileCreate, so a FileCreate call with an empty path falls into the permissive catch-all and counts as grounded — contradicting the file's own docstring 45 lines below, which states all three should ground on their path.

Mediumcrates/lumen-store/src/repositories/queue.rs:78–95
Dead-letter classification has a read-modify-write race

mark_failed reads retry_count, computes +1 in Rust, and writes it back as an absolute value across two separate autocommit statements with no transaction. Concurrent callers can both read the same stale count and both write the same incremented value, undercounting real failures. .unwrap_or(0) additionally treats any SELECT error (not just "no row") as "count is zero," which can reset an already-failing job's counter. No production caller exists yet.

MediumAGENTS.md:31 · workspace Cargo.toml
The one rule marked CRITICAL has zero enforcement

The layer-licensing boundary ("Layer 1/1.5 must not depend on Layer 2/4," a real FSL-license containment rule) rests on convention alone. There's no deny.toml, no cargo-deny bans step, and no CI at all — .github/ doesn't exist. just ci only runs if a developer opts in via just hooks. Adding one dependency line would silently relicense a permissive crate.

MediumAGENTS.md invariant 3 · test_analysis_pipeline.rs:288
The "no nested heap allocations" invariant is unenforceable by construction

Enforcing it mechanically would require a #[global_allocator] guard, which needs unsafe impl — forbidden by invariant 1. The test suite's own comment documents the harness as "NOT IMPLEMENTED" and names live violations already present (a per-turn BTreeMap collect in pr_link.rs, a format! allocation in circuit_breaker.rs). Two stated invariants are in direct tension.

Mediumcrates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs:123
1-hour cache tier is permanently zero, and the discount ratio it's supposed to encode isn't consistent

ephemeral_1h_tokens is hardcoded to 0 — no signal populates it anywhere. AGENTS.md's "deterministic token accounting" invariant implies a single cache-read discount ratio; the seed table actually varies it per model (0.10× for Anthropic, 0.25× for Gemini Flash, 0.14× for GLM), which the invariant's wording doesn't account for.

Mediumclaude.rs:295 · agy.rs:183 · codex.rs:152 · opencode.rs:202
A fresh PricingTable is allocated on every single parse call

TokenEconomics::calculate takes &PricingTable specifically so callers can reuse one — every real call site instead does &PricingTable::seed() inline, rebuilding a ~40-row Vec on every adapter invocation. Not yet measured as a bottleneck, but a real, avoidable allocation the API was designed to let callers skip.

Mediumcrates/lumen-session/src/adapter.rs:10
Dead API surface that misleads callers

IngestionError::MalformedJson(String) is declared but constructed nowhere. Every adapter's real behavior on a bad line is silent-skip or, since this session, a ParseFailureRecord — never this variant. A caller pattern-matching on IngestionError will write dead-code branches for it.

Mediumcrates/lumen-model — TokenEconomics::calculate signature change
The breaking pricing API change has no migration note

claude.rs and opencode.rs carry zero /// doc comments. The 5-argument → per-turn-slice signature change has no changelog entry, no deprecation shim, nothing pointing a downstream maintainer toward TurnPricingInput. This is exactly the change that will break Prism's build the moment it updates — see the note below.

Mediumcrates/lumen-analysis/src/engine.rs:121–125
The full accumulator pipeline runs per subagent to keep one field

Every subagent transcript runs the complete recursive process_transcript — all 19 accumulators — and only .attribution survives into by_subagent. The type signature makes this an intentional narrowing, not silent data loss, but it's real computational waste at recursion depth, worth revisiting if subagent-heavy sessions become common.

Mediumcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs:144–145
Codex cache tokens are hardcoded to zero

cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens are always 0 in Codex's TurnPricingInput — no cache-related key is ever probed in the token_count payload. Unresolved: no real Codex session fixture exists in the repo to confirm whether Codex's actual wire format even carries cache-token data, so this may be dead code rather than data loss — flagged as an open question, not a confirmed bug.

Mediumcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs:109
Open question: is_sidechain may not match real Claude Code's field name

The sidechain-exclusion filter reads is_sidechain (snake_case); every fixture in the repo uses that spelling too — but no fixture in this codebase has been checked against a real, live Claude Code JSONL export. If the real field is isSidechain (camelCase), CRIT-LUMEN-026's entire subagent-exclusion mechanism never fires in production, silently contaminating the main transcript with subagent turns. pricing & economics

SPEC-LUMEN-002-SESSION
Claude / AGY / Codex adapters, in scope
11 / 15 6 / 15 3 genuine divergences, 3 correct-but-unproven-by-test.

Notecrates/lumen-cli
The CLI never actually calls lumen-store or lumen-analysis

Highcrates/lumen-pattern/src/lib.rs:94–100
Correction: file-only cycles close internally, then get silently dropped from reporting

Earlier in this session, calculate_monotonicity's back-edge fix (target_last_seen) was verified against its spec and reported as working. code-review's sweep pass found the gap that verification missed: push_tool closes a cycle using target_symbol.or(target_file), but detect_circular_loops only reports one using target_symbol — if let Some(sym) = first_symbol silently drops any cycle whose nodes are grounded on target_file alone. Three or more repeated reads of the same file — a real, common redundant-exploration pattern — close a cycle internally and then vanish before reaching CircularLoopAnomaly. calculate_monotonicity reports a perfect 1.0 for exactly the loop this session's own grounding work was meant to catch.

Highcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs:80
Codex sessions built from response_item lines silently parse as empty

Both detect_orchestrator and CodexAdapter::matches_fingerprint accept "type":"response_item" as valid Codex content — a real rollout format. But parse_stream unconditionally skips any line whose top-level type isn't exactly "event_msg". A real Codex file composed mostly of response_item lines is correctly identified as Codex, then silently parsed into a transcript with zero turns, a default session id, and zero economics — the same "successful but fake" failure mode as the CLI's fallback bug above, but triggered by a format the adapter itself claims to support.

Highcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/agy.rs:144
Tool-call and tool-result IDs are minted from two different counters that never agree

CanonicalToolCall.call_id is minted from a local tool_calls.len() counter that resets to zero every PLANNER_RESPONSE turn; the following TOOL_RESULT reconstructs its call_id from the global turns.len().saturating_sub(1) — a different number space entirely. Per the adapter's own fixture: a call gets id "agy_call_0", and the result that's supposed to match it computes "agy_call_1", matching no call ever created. Every call↔result correlation for Antigravity sessions is broken — compounding the structural tool_calls/tool_results gap above with a second, AGY-specific way for the same correlation to fail.

input.new_string:

Mediumcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs:36
Codex's wall-clock duration is always zero

started_at is set once to Utc::now() (the moment the parser runs) and never updated from a real log timestamp, unlike the other three adapters, which all track a has_start flag. Since real logs are historical, ended_at - started_at is always negative and clamps to 0 — every Codex session's wall_duration_ms/active_duration_ms is silently zero, untouched by any test.

Mediumcrates/lumen-pattern/src/lib.rs:202
Version-control mutation detection never matches a real command

ground_tool_intent's mutation check compares the entire raw command string against bare verb literals (action == "commit" || action == "push"), but both adapters that build ToolIntent::VersionControl store the full command line — "git commit -m 'fix bug'", never a bare "commit". The comparison never matches, so is_mutation is false for essentially every real commit or push, undercounting total_mutations and skewing the monotonicity/efficiency scores that are lumen-pattern's whole purpose. Untested — the existing graph tests construct ToolNode directly, bypassing this function entirely.

Mediumcrates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/token_usage.rs:65
Per-model token breakdown is tracked correctly, then thrown away

update_raw correctly splits usage into a real per-model map as messages arrive. finalize() never reads it — it calls TokenEconomics::calculate with only the grand totals and a single default_model, so a session using two real models (e.g. Haiku and Sonnet in the same session) ends up with one merged entry, silently mis-attributing one model's usage to the other. The existing test only ever feeds a single model, so the discard is invisible to it.

Mediumcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/opencode.rs:87
Pure cache-hit turns are dropped entirely

Cache-token accumulation is gated behind in_tok > 0 || out_tok > 0 — a condition that never inspects the cache values it's supposed to guard. A usage object reporting only cache activity (input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0, cache_read_input_tokens: 5000) fails the gate outright, so a real 5,000-token cache read is silently never recorded, undercounting cache_hit_ratio and total_cost_usd.

Mediumcrates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/context_growth.rs:36
A real zero-token turn is indistinguishable from "no previous turn yet"

previous_prompt_tokens uses plain 0u64 as both its "nothing seen yet" sentinel and a legitimate zero-token reading. A turn sequence like [500, 0, 5000] loses the real 5,000-token jump after turn 3, because the growth guard requires previous_prompt_tokens > 0 — which a genuine zero-token turn defeats just as effectively as an absent one. Untested against a real zero-valued usage turn.

Mediumcrates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs:297
provided_cost_usd is checked for null but never actually read

The explicit-null guard added this session checks costUSD for a literal null — implying the field is meant to feed TokenEconomics.provided_cost_usd, the twin-field mechanism built specifically to hold a source's own reported cost. It's never wired up: provided_cost_usd is unconditionally None at the construction site. The drift-detection half of that mechanism doesn't exist yet for Claude Code, the one adapter with a real cost field to compare against.

input.description: Fix pricing model-string normalization
input.prompt:
Execute this bug fix via the full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). This is fix #1 of a prioritized sequence addressing findings from an adversarial review (published as an artifact, not a formal spec@1) — no plan@1/spec_file_path exists for this work, proceed directly from the finding description below.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen (Rust cargo workspace). Baseline confirmed clean: `cargo test --workspace` passes 96/96.

## The bug (Blocker #1 from the review)

`PricingTable::rate_for` in crates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs (around line 118-135) matches model names by EXACT string equality against PricingTable::seed()'s short canonical keys (e.g. "claude-3-5-sonnet", "claude-opus", "gpt-4o", "gemini-2.0-flash"). But real adapters pass raw, provider-versioned model strings that never match those keys exactly:
- ClaudeCodeAdapter (crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs) reads a real `message.model` field from the JSONL, e.g. "claude-3-5-haiku-20241022" or "claude-opus-4-20250514" or "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022".
- Real GPT-4o strings look like "gpt-4o-2024-08-06".
- Real Gemini strings look like "gemini-2.0-flash-001" or "gemini-2.0-flash-exp".

Verified by direct execution: rate_for("claude-3-5-haiku-20241022", ...), rate_for("claude-opus-4-20250514", ...), rate_for("gpt-4o-2024-08-06", ...), and rate_for("gemini-2.0-flash-001", ...) all currently return Claude 3.5 Sonnet's rates ($3.00/$3.75/$0.30/$15.00 per M) via the CRIT-LUMEN-008 unrecognized-model fallback, instead of each model's own correct seeded rate. The spec's own PricingTable api_surface entry (specs/SPEC-LUMEN-001-MODEL.json, the "PricingRate / PricingTable" entry) already states: "model matching normalizes raw provider-versioned strings (e.g. \"claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\") to the seeded canonical keys (e.g. \"claude-3-5-sonnet\")" -- this normalization was promised but never implemented.

## The fix

Add a normalization step to PricingTable::rate_for (or a private helper function it calls) that strips known provider-versioning patterns from a raw model string down to its canonical seeded key, BEFORE doing the model_recognized/exact-match lookup. Read crates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs first to see the exact current seed() keys you need to normalize toward -- do not guess, read the actual seeded model key strings (they include at minimum: claude-3-5-sonnet, claude-3-5-haiku, claude-opus, qwen-2.5-coder, gpt-4o, deepseek-r1, kimi-k1.5, glm-4-plus, gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.0-pro -- confirm the exact list and exact spelling from the file itself).

Design the normalization to handle the real patterns that actually occur:
1. A trailing date suffix like "-20241022" or "-2024-08-06" or "-001" or "-exp" appended to an otherwise-exact-match prefix.
2. Case where the raw string, after stripping a trailing date/version suffix, exactly equals a seeded key -- that's the primary case to solve. Use a real, defensible algorithm (e.g. strip a trailing `-YYYYMMDD` or `-YYYY-MM-DD` pattern via a helper, or try progressively shorter prefixes split on '-' against the seeded key set) rather than a giant hardcoded lookup table of every version string that will immediately go stale -- but if you judge a small explicit alias table is more correct and maintainable than a fragile suffix-stripping regex, that's an acceptable engineering call; explain your choice in the commit message.
3. Do NOT break the existing CRIT-LUMEN-008 behavior: a genuinely unrecognized model (one that doesn't normalize to ANY seeded key) must still fall back to claude-3-5-sonnet's rate, exactly as before.
4. Do NOT break CRIT-LUMEN-161: a recognized model missing one specific rate kind (e.g. Qwen has no CacheWrite row) must still return 0.0 for that kind, not fall back to Sonnet.

## TDD steps

1. Write a new failing test in crates/lumen-model/tests/test_pricing.rs (add to the existing file, don't replace it) that calls rate_for with REAL provider-versioned strings and asserts the CORRECT model-specific rate is returned, not Sonnet's fallback rate. Cover at minimum: "claude-3-5-haiku-20241022" -> Haiku's rates, "claude-opus-4-20250514" -> Opus's rates, "gpt-4o-2024-08-06" -> GPT-4o's rates, "gemini-2.0-flash-001" -> Gemini 2.0 Flash's rates. Also add a test proving a genuinely unrecognized model string (e.g. "totally-fake-model-xyz-99999999") still falls back to Sonnet's rates (CRIT-LUMEN-008 preserved), and a test proving qwen-2.5-coder's missing CacheWrite kind still returns 0.0, not a substituted rate (CRIT-LUMEN-161 preserved).
2. Confirm red: run the new test, confirm it fails against the current unmodified pricing.rs (returns Sonnet's rate instead of the correct model's rate).
3. Implement the normalization fix in pricing.rs.
4. Confirm green: the new test passes, AND run the full existing test_pricing.rs suite (all prior tests, including CRIT-LUMEN-008/161 tests) to confirm no regression.
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-model` fully, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions across the whole workspace (other crates construct PricingTable/call rate_for too -- check crates/lumen-session's adapters and any other real caller for behavior that might change).
6. Commit with a clear message explaining the fix and referencing this being the root-cause fix for the "no model-string normalization" finding.

Stay scoped to pricing.rs and its own test file for this task -- do NOT also fix the separate finding that AgyAdapter/OpenCodeAdapter/CodexAdapter never reassign model_family from a real parsed value (that's tracked as a separate, later fix). This task is specifically about making rate_for itself correctly normalize whatever real model string it's given.

Report: test results, exact normalization algorithm chosen and why, and confirmation of zero regressions.

input.description: Fix Codex service_tier zeroing session cost
input.prompt:
Execute this bug fix via the full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). This is fix #2 of a prioritized sequence addressing findings from an adversarial review (published as an artifact, not a formal spec@1) — no plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from the finding description below.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen (Rust cargo workspace). Baseline: fix #1 (commit cb29996) just landed, adding PricingTable::normalize_model_key -- rate_for now normalizes raw model strings before its exact-match lookup, called at pricing.rs line ~151. Read the CURRENT pricing.rs before starting, since line numbers have shifted from before fix #1.

## The bug (Blocker #2 from the review)

`PricingTable::seed()` pushes every PricingRate row with `tier: None`. `rate_for`'s filter requires `r.tier.as_deref() == tier` (exact match). When CodexAdapter sets `tier: Some("Standard")` on a TurnPricingInput (from a real `thread_settings_applied` event -- crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs around line 148), the tier filter matches ZERO rows for every TokenRateKind, and `unwrap_or(0.0)` silently returns $0.00 for input/output/cache-write/cache-read. This means ANY Codex session that reports a service_tier (which real Codex sessions commonly do) gets priced at exactly $0.00 regardless of actual token volume. The shipped Codex test fixture (crates/lumen-fixtures/src/corpus/codex.rs) already carries `service_tier: "Standard"`, and no existing test asserts total_cost_usd for it -- so this is currently invisible to the suite.

## The fix

In `PricingTable::rate_for`, when a caller passes `Some(tier)` and no row matches that specific tier (for the already-normalized/recognized model + kind + as_of), fall back to searching that same model's `tier: None` rows before giving up and returning 0.0. This must NOT change behavior for:
- A model with a real tiered row that DOES match -- that should still win over any None-tier fallback (tier-specific pricing takes priority when it exists).
- CRIT-LUMEN-161's behavior: a recognized model missing a specific *rate kind* entirely (e.g. Qwen's absent CacheWrite row) must still return 0.0 for that kind -- this is a different case from "recognized model, tier requested, no tiered row exists but an untiered row does." Read the current code carefully to keep these two fallback paths distinct: (1) unrecognized model -> Sonnet fallback (existing), (2) recognized model + tier requested + no tiered row -> fall back to that model's own tier:None row (new, this fix), (3) recognized model + specific kind entirely absent even after tier fallback -> 0.0 (existing, must still work).

Read the exact current `rate_for` implementation first -- do not guess at the existing branch structure, since fix #1 already modified it.

## TDD steps

1. Add a failing test to crates/lumen-model/tests/test_pricing.rs asserting: a PricingTable containing only tier:None rows for "gpt-4o" (or reuse PricingTable::seed()), when queried via rate_for("gpt-4o", Some("Standard"), TokenRateKind::Input, as_of), returns the SAME non-zero rate as rate_for("gpt-4o", None, TokenRateKind::Input, as_of) -- i.e. the tier:None row's rate, not 0.0. Also add/keep a test proving that when a tier-specific row DOES exist and matches, it's preferred over the tier:None fallback (construct a hand-built PricingTable with both a tier:None row and a tier:Some("Standard") row at a higher rate for the same model/kind, and confirm rate_for(model, Some("Standard"), kind, as_of) returns the tiered rate, not the untiered one). Also keep/add a test confirming CRIT-LUMEN-161 still holds: qwen-2.5-coder's missing CacheWrite kind still returns exactly 0.0 even after this fix (not silently picking up some other fallback).
2. Confirm red against the current (fix-#1-updated) pricing.rs.
3. Implement the tier-fallback fix in rate_for.
4. Confirm green: new tests pass, full existing test_pricing.rs suite passes with no regression.
5. Also add a test in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_codex.rs (or wherever the existing Codex fixture test lives) asserting that the real_codex_session_dump() fixture -- which carries service_tier: "Standard" -- now produces a non-zero total_cost_usd when parsed by CodexAdapter, proving the fix closes the real, end-to-end bug (not just the pricing.rs unit level). Read the current test_codex.rs first to see how economics is currently asserted (or not) there.
6. Run `cargo test -p lumen-model`, `cargo test -p lumen-session`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
7. Commit with a message explaining the fix.

Stay scoped to pricing.rs, its tests, and the Codex fixture-level test. Do not touch other adapters.

Report: test results and confirmation of zero regressions, including the real total_cost_usd value now produced by the Codex fixture.

input.description: Fix cross-turn tool call/result correlation
input.prompt:
Execute this bug fix via the full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). Fix #3 of a prioritized sequence from an adversarial review (no plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from this brief). This is the review's one "architectural" finding — it comes with an exact design already worked out from reading the real code, follow it precisely rather than re-deriving your own approach.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: fixes #1 (cb29996) and #2 (79bd0f2) landed clean, `cargo test --workspace` green.

## The bug

`CanonicalTurn` (crates/lumen-model/src/turn.rs) can hold both `tool_calls: SmallVec<[CanonicalToolCall; 2]>` and `tool_results: SmallVec<[CanonicalToolResult; 2]>`, but NO real adapter (claude.rs, agy.rs, codex.rs, opencode.rs) ever populates both on the same turn -- a tool call and its result always land on separate turns (call on an assistant turn, result on a following ToolResult turn). Both `CanonicalToolCall` and `CanonicalToolResult` carry a `call_id: CompactString` meant to correlate them; `CanonicalToolResult` also carries `is_error: bool` and `truncated_output: Option<CompactString>`.

Two accumulators in crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/ assume same-turn correlation and are broken as a result:

1. **trajectory_dag.rs** (`TrajectoryDagAccumulator::update`, current file has ~60 lines): for each call in `entry.tool_calls`, it searches `entry.tool_results` (the SAME turn) for a matching `call_id` to set `ToolNode.had_error`. Since results never share a turn with their call, this `.find(...)` always returns `None`, so `had_error` is `false` for every node in every real session, including calls that genuinely errored.

2. **pr_link.rs** (`PrLinkAccumulator::update`, current file has ~97 lines): builds `call_intents` from `entry.tool_calls` (the SAME turn) only when `!entry.tool_results.is_empty()`, then checks `entry.tool_results` against it to set `linked_via_vcs_tool`. Same problem -- `call_intents` is always empty when there are actually results to check, so `linked_via_vcs_tool` never increments, ever.

## The fix (already designed against the real code -- follow this)

Both fixes follow the same pattern: buffer call metadata in a field that persists ACROSS the whole single forward pass over turns (not scoped to one `entry`), so a call seen on turn N can still be found when its result arrives on turn N+5. This preserves the workspace's single-pass-over-turns streaming discipline -- it's a bounded in-flight buffer, not a full-transcript pre-scan.

**trajectory_dag.rs:**
- Add a field to `TrajectoryDagAccumulator`, e.g. `pending_calls: std::collections::HashMap<CompactString, usize>` (call_id -> index into `self.nodes`).
- When a call is processed: push the `ToolNode` with `had_error: false` as today, then `self.pending_calls.insert(call.call_id.clone(), self.nodes.len() - 1);`.
- Add a SEPARATE loop over `entry.tool_results` that runs on EVERY turn (not gated on that turn also having tool_calls): for each result, `if let Some(&idx) = self.pending_calls.get(&result.call_id) { self.nodes[idx].had_error = result.is_error; self.pending_calls.remove(&result.call_id); }`.
- Remove the now-dead same-turn `.find(...)` lookup entirely.

**pr_link.rs:**
- Add a field to `PrLinkAccumulator`, e.g. `pending_vcs_calls: std::collections::BTreeSet<CompactString>` (call_ids of calls whose intent was `ToolIntent::VersionControl`; a set is enough, you don't need the full intent).
- When processing `entry.tool_calls` (on every turn, not gated): for each call whose `intent` matches `ToolIntent::VersionControl { .. }`, insert its `call_id` into `pending_vcs_calls`.
- Change the results loop to run on every turn (drop the `if !entry.tool_results.is_empty()` gate around the call_intents construction -- keep it, if you want, purely as a short-circuit around the whole results loop, but the vcs-call bookkeeping must not depend on it), and check `self.pending_vcs_calls.contains(&result.call_id)` instead of the current turn-scoped `call_intents` map. Remove a call_id from the set once matched, if you want to avoid unbounded growth, though it's optional since call_ids should be unique per session.

Read the CURRENT exact content of both files first (they may have shifted slightly from this description) before editing -- this is a precise description of the current logic, not a guess, but confirm line-for-line before changing anything.

## Test coverage gap to fix as part of this task

A test at crates/lumen-analysis/tests/test_accumulators.rs (search for line ~1447, or search for `had_error` and `linked_via_vcs_tool` assertions) currently ASSERTS the broken always-false/always-zero behavior as if it were correct -- i.e. it builds calls and results on separate turns and then asserts `had_error == false` / `linked_via_vcs_tool == 0` as the EXPECTED outcome. Find this test (or these tests) and rewrite the assertions to reflect CORRECT cross-turn correlation: a call on one turn whose result (on a later turn) has `is_error: true` should produce `had_error == true`; a VersionControl call whose result turn contains a PR URL should increment `linked_via_vcs_tool`. Do not just delete the test -- invert its assertion to prove the fix, matching the pattern of a real call/result pair split across two turns (this is the actual, common shape every real adapter produces).

## TDD steps

1. Read crates/lumen-analysis/src/accumulators/trajectory_dag.rs, pr_link.rs, and the relevant section of test_accumulators.rs in full.
2. Write/rewrite failing tests: for trajectory_dag, a two-turn sequence (turn N: assistant turn with a tool_call; turn N+1: ToolResult turn with a matching call_id and is_error: true) asserting the resulting ToolNode has had_error == true. For pr_link, a two-turn sequence (turn N: assistant turn with a VersionControl tool_call; turn N+1: ToolResult turn with matching call_id whose truncated_output contains a real github.com/{owner}/{repo}/pull/{digits} URL) asserting linked_via_vcs_tool == 1. Confirm both are red against the current (unfixed) accumulators.
3. Implement both fixes exactly as designed above.
4. Confirm green: new tests pass, and the full existing test_accumulators.rs suite (all other accumulator tests) still passes with no regression -- especially any pre-existing trajectory_dag/pr_link tests that may have been asserting same-turn behavior; check whether those need updating too (a real adapter never produces same-turn call+result, but a hand-built test fixture might have -- if such a test exists and asserts genuinely same-turn correlation, it should still work correctly under the new logic since the pending-map approach also handles same-turn matches; if it doesn't, that's a real second bug to flag, not paper over).
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-analysis`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit both files together as one commit (this is one root-cause fix spanning two files, not two independent changes) with a message explaining the structural nature of the fix.

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, and explicit confirmation that the previously-inverted test now correctly proves the fix rather than the bug.

## The bug (Blocker from the review)

crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs's `load_session` function (currently around line 54-74):

```rust
fn load_session(path: &Path) -> Result<CanonicalTranscript> {
    let file = File::open(path).into_diagnostic()?;
    let reader = BufReader::new(file);
    let mut sample_file = File::open(path).into_diagnostic()?;
    let mut buffer = [0u8; 2048];
    use std::io::Read;
    let n = sample_file.read(&mut buffer).unwrap_or(0);
    let sample = &buffer[..n];
    let orchestrator = detect_orchestrator(sample).unwrap_or(OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode);
    match orchestrator {
        OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode => ClaudeCodeAdapter.parse_stream(Box::new(reader)).into_diagnostic(),
        OrchestratorKind::Antigravity => AgyAdapter.parse_stream(Box::new(reader)).into_diagnostic(),
        OrchestratorKind::Codex => CodexAdapter.parse_stream(Box::new(reader)).into_diagnostic(),
        OrchestratorKind::OpenCode => OpenCodeAdapter.parse_stream(Box::new(reader)).into_diagnostic(),
        _ => ClaudeCodeAdapter.parse_stream(Box::new(reader)).into_diagnostic(),
    }
}
```

`detect_orchestrator(sample).unwrap_or(OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode)` means: when fingerprinting genuinely fails to recognize the file (returns `None` -- any Kimi session, any GenericOtel session, a malformed/empty file), the CLI silently GUESSES ClaudeCode instead of surfacing that the format is unrecognized. `ClaudeCodeAdapter::parse_stream` cannot fail on wrong-schema JSON input -- every field extraction defaults quietly (`.get(...).and_then(...).unwrap_or(...)` throughout claude.rs) -- so it returns `Ok(CanonicalTranscript)` with zero turns, `session_id: "unknown"`, and a full $0.0000 economics table. This is the crate's real production binary: `lumen scan` silently counts each such file as a "discovered session" and `lumen audit`/`lumen trace` exit 0 with a clean-looking, entirely fabricated report on a file it never actually understood.

There's a second instance of the same defect: the `_ => ClaudeCodeAdapter...` catch-all arm (line ~72) means any `OrchestratorKind` variant this match doesn't explicitly handle (e.g. `Kimi`, `GenericOtel` -- check the real enum in crates/lumen-model/src/transcript.rs for the full current variant list) ALSO silently falls back to ClaudeCodeAdapter instead of surfacing "recognized as X, but no parser exists for X yet."

## The fix

`crates/lumen-session/src/adapter.rs` already declares `IngestionError::UnrecognizedFormat` -- it's just never actually returned anywhere. Use it:

1. When `detect_orchestrator(sample)` returns `None`, `load_session` should return `Err(...)` wrapping `IngestionError::UnrecognizedFormat` (via `.into_diagnostic()` or however the file's existing error-conversion pattern works -- read the file's current `Result<T>` type alias / miette usage first) instead of defaulting to `OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode`. Include the file path in the error context so a real user gets a useful message (miette's `.into_diagnostic()` plus a `.wrap_err(...)`-style addition if that pattern is available in this codebase's dependencies -- check what's actually imported/used elsewhere in main.rs for adding context to a Result before inventing a new pattern).
2. The `_ => ` catch-all arm should likewise return an error (e.g. a clear message that the orchestrator was recognized by fingerprint but has no implemented adapter) rather than silently parsing with ClaudeCodeAdapter. Do NOT delete OrchestratorKind variants or add new match arms for adapters that don't exist -- just make the fallback arm fail loudly instead of silently mis-parsing.
3. `cmd_scan` (around line 164-179) already does `if let Ok(transcript) = load_session(&path) { sessions.push(transcript); }` -- once `load_session` correctly returns `Err` for unrecognized files, this already does the right thing (silently skips the file from the discovered-sessions count) with NO code change needed there. Confirm this is true by reading cmd_scan's current code; do not change it unless you find it's actually wrong.

Judgment call, decide based on what you find: the review separately suggested "reject a transcript that produced zero turns from non-empty input" as an additional defense-in-depth check. This is optional and riskier (a legitimate session with genuinely zero turns is a real, already-tested case -- check for an existing "empty session" test in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_claude.rs before doing anything here). Only add this secondary check if you can do it without breaking that existing empty-session contract; if it's not clearly safe, skip it and just fix the primary unwrap_or(ClaudeCode) bug, which is the actual confirmed defect.

## Testing

crates/lumen-cli currently has NO test directory (`crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs` only, no `tests/`, no `lib.rs`). Since it's a binary-only crate, integration tests in a separate `tests/` directory can't link against its private functions. Add tests via an inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` block directly in main.rs (a pattern already used elsewhere in this workspace, e.g. crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs) that calls `load_session` directly against a real temp file (use the `tempfile` crate if it's already a dev-dependency somewhere reachable, or write to `std::env::temp_dir()` and clean up -- check what's actually available to this crate's Cargo.toml first, add `tempfile` as a dev-dependency if needed).

TDD steps:
1. Write a failing test: write a genuinely unrecognized-format file (e.g. a JSON object with no sessionId/parentUuid/step_index/event_msg/SQLite-header markers -- something detect_orchestrator would return None for) to a temp path, call `load_session` on it, and assert the result is `Err`. Confirm this is red against the current code (currently returns `Ok` with a fake empty transcript).
2. Implement the fix.
3. Confirm green.
4. Also add a positive-path regression test confirming `load_session` still correctly parses a real, recognizable Claude Code fixture (reuse `lumen_fixtures::real_claude_session_dump()` if lumen-cli can reasonably add lumen-fixtures as a dev-dependency, or construct a minimal valid sample inline) and returns `Ok` -- proving the fix doesn't break the legitimate path.
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-cli`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit.

Report: test results, exact error-handling pattern used, and confirmation the legitimate parse path still works.

use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};
use compact_str::CompactString;
use lumen_model::{OrchestratorKind, TokenEconomics};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct QueuedSessionRow {
    pub id: i64,
    pub provider: String,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub source_path: String,
    pub source_hash: u64,
    pub retry_count: u32,
    pub status: String,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SessionFactRecord {
    pub provider: String,
    pub provider_session_id: String,
    pub model_family: String,
    pub orchestrator: OrchestratorKind,
    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub ended_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    pub wall_duration_ms: u64,
    pub turn_count: usize,
    pub economics: TokenEconomics,
    pub has_anomalies: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SessionSummaryReadModel {
    pub id: i64,
    pub provider: String,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub model_family: String,
    pub turn_count: usize,
    pub wall_duration_ms: u64,
    pub cache_hit_ratio: f32,
    pub total_cost_usd: f64,
    pub net_savings_usd: f64,
    pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SessionDetailReadModel {
    pub summary: SessionSummaryReadModel,
    pub economics: TokenEconomics,
    pub tool_counts: BTreeMap<CompactString, usize>,
    pub error_counts: BTreeMap<CompactString, usize>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct SessionFilter {
    pub provider: Option<String>,
    pub limit: usize,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FindingFactRecord {
    pub rule_id: String,
    pub severity: String,
    pub confidence: f32,
    pub title: String,
    pub message: String,
    pub evidence_json: Option<serde_json::Value>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct FindingReadModel {
    pub id: i64,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub rule_id: String,
    pub severity: String,
    pub confidence: f32,
    pub title: String,
    pub message: String,
}

input.prompt:
Execute via full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). This implements RollupRepository from specs/SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE.json, covering CRIT-LUMEN-120, CRIT-LUMEN-121, CRIT-LUMEN-122. Read these three criteria's exact wording from specs/SPEC-LUMEN-003-STORE.json before starting, and read the "RollupRepository" api_surface entry in the same file for the exact signature.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: ToolCallRepository just landed (commit 1113f8e), `cargo test --workspace` green. Read crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/findings.rs and the newly-added crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/tool_call.rs first for the established repository pattern. Read crates/lumen-store/src/models.rs for where FactRecord/ReadModel types belong, and crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/mod.rs for the module re-export pattern.

The `rollups` table already exists (migration V5 in crates/lumen-store/src/migrations.rs): columns id, period_start TIMESTAMP, period_type TEXT, session_count, total_cost_usd, total_savings_usd, total_duration_ms. It has NO unique constraint on (period_start, period_type).

## What to build

1. Add a NEW migration V6 to `MigrationManager::MIGRATIONS` in crates/lumen-store/src/migrations.rs (append as a new array element -- SQLite has no ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT, and CRIT-LUMEN-120 explicitly requires this be a new migration, never editing the already-applied V5 migration in place): `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_rollups_period ON rollups(period_start, period_type);`. Verify apply_migrations' existing versioning logic (idx+1 based) picks this up correctly as version 6 with no other changes needed.

2. In crates/lumen-store/src/models.rs, add `RollupFactRecord` (period_start: DateTime<Utc>, period_type: String, session_count: usize/i64, total_cost_usd: f64, total_savings_usd: f64, total_duration_ms: u64 -- match Rust idiom used elsewhere) and `RollupReadModel` (id: i64, plus the same fields).

3. Create crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/rollup.rs implementing `RollupRepository<'a>` per the exact spec signature:
   - `pub fn new(conn: &'a Connection) -> Self`
   - `pub fn upsert_rollup(&self, record: &RollupFactRecord) -> Result<(), StoreError>` -- INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(period_start, period_type) DO UPDATE SET ... (idempotent upsert, relies on the V6 unique index; mirror SessionRepository::upsert_session's ON CONFLICT pattern).
   - `pub fn get_rollup(&self, period_start: DateTime<Utc>, period_type: &str) -> Result<Option<RollupReadModel>, StoreError>` -- returns Ok(None) if no matching row (CRIT-LUMEN-121), not an error.
   - `pub fn list_rollups(&self, period_type: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<RollupReadModel>, StoreError>` -- filters by period_type, ORDER BY period_start DESC, LIMIT (CRIT-LUMEN-122).

4. Add `pub mod rollup; pub use rollup::RollupRepository;` to crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/mod.rs.

## TDD steps

1. Write failing tests in crates/lumen-store/tests/test_store.rs (add to the existing file):
   - test that upsert_rollup called twice with identical (period_start, period_type) but different session_count/cost values results in exactly ONE row with the updated values (idempotent upsert, CRIT-LUMEN-120) -- this will fail with a UNIQUE constraint error or a duplicate row unless the V6 migration + ON CONFLICT clause are both correct.
   - test that get_rollup with a non-matching (period_start, period_type) returns Ok(None), not an error (CRIT-LUMEN-121).
   - test that list_rollups with a given period_type and limit returns only matching rows, ordered by period_start descending, respecting the limit (CRIT-LUMEN-122) -- insert at least 3 rollups across two different period_types with different period_start values to make the filter/order/limit assertions meaningful.
2. Confirm red against the current codebase.
3. Implement.
4. Confirm green: new tests pass, full crates/lumen-store test suite passes with no regression. Specifically verify the migration count assertion (if any test checks `run_migrations` returns a specific applied_count) is updated for the new V6 migration -- check crates/lumen-store/tests/test_store.rs and test_store_concurrency.rs for any hardcoded migration count and update it if the count changes for a fresh database.
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-store`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit.

Report: test results and confirmation of zero regressions, including whether any migration-count assertion needed updating.

In crates/lumen-store/src/models.rs, add `CommandEventFactRecord` (command_base: String, sanitized_args: Option<String>, is_error: bool) and `CommandEventReadModel` (id: i64, session_id: String or i64 -- check whether this repository keys by the string provider_session_id or the internal integer id; the spec's signature says `insert_command_events(&self, session_id: &str, events: &[CommandEventFactRecord])` -- note this takes session_id as &str, UNLIKE ToolCallRepository which took an i64. Read the spec's exact CommandEventRepository api_surface signature again to confirm this before writing code -- do not assume it matches ToolCallRepository's convention just because they're structurally similar tables).

   - `pub fn list_by_session(&self, session_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<CommandEventReadModel>, StoreError>` -- same session_id resolution consideration as insert.

3. Add `pub mod command_event; pub use command_event::CommandEventRepository;` to crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/mod.rs.

1. Write failing tests in crates/lumen-store/tests/test_store.rs (add to the existing file):
   - test that insert_command_events with a non-empty slice inserts the right row count for a real, previously-upserted session (use SessionRepository::upsert_session first to create a real session row, matching whatever pattern existing tests in this file already use to set up a session before testing session-scoped repositories).
   - test that an empty slice inserts zero rows without error.
   - test that list_by_session returns the correct CommandEventReadModel rows, with sanitized_args round-tripping correctly (including the None case).
   - test that insert_command_events / list_by_session against a session_id that doesn't exist in the sessions table behaves sensibly (returns an error, per your documented design choice above) rather than panicking or silently corrupting data.
2. Confirm red against the current codebase.
3. Implement.
4. Confirm green: new tests pass, full crates/lumen-store test suite passes with no regression.
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-store`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit.

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, and the session_id resolution/error-handling design you chose for the nonexistent-session case.

input.description: Fix fingerprint parity and UTF-8 truncation
input.prompt:
Execute via full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). Two related High-severity findings from an adversarial review, both in crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs and its four adapter consumers. No plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from this brief.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: 5 Blocker fixes landed (commits cb29996..0681148), `cargo test --workspace` green (121 tests).

## Bug 1: matches_fingerprint / detect_orchestrator drift

`detect_orchestrator` in crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs is an ORDERED if-chain (ClaudeCode -> Antigravity -> Codex -> OpenCode checked in that order, first match wins). Each adapter's own `matches_fingerprint(&self, sample: &str) -> bool` (claude.rs:16-21, codex.rs:16-19, opencode.rs:16-21, agy.rs:24-29) independently re-implements a similar-looking boolean condition with NO awareness of that precedence. Two concrete problems:
1. `ClaudeCodeAdapter::matches_fingerprint` (claude.rs:16-21) still checks the OLD, looser condition (`sessionId && (permission-mode || leafUuid || parentUuid)`) while `detect_orchestrator`'s ClaudeCode branch was tightened this session to require `sessionId && parentUuid` together. These two now genuinely disagree on inputs like `{"sessionId":"x","leafUuid":"y"}` (no parentUuid): matches_fingerprint says true, detect_orchestrator says false.
2. Even where the OTHER three adapters' matches_fingerprint conditions currently happen to textually match detect_orchestrator's corresponding branch, a sample matching BOTH an earlier and a later branch's markers (e.g. one containing both Claude Code AND Codex markers) makes detect_orchestrator return the FIRST match (ClaudeCode) while a later adapter's standalone matches_fingerprint (no precedence awareness) can ALSO return true for its own condition -- both can claim it simultaneously.

## The fix

Read the current, exact `detect_orchestrator` function in crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs first. Then change ALL FOUR adapters' `matches_fingerprint` methods to delegate directly to `detect_orchestrator` instead of maintaining an independent boolean expression:

```rust
fn matches_fingerprint(&self, sample: &str) -> bool {
    detect_orchestrator(sample.as_bytes()) == Some(OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode) // (or Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode as appropriate per adapter)
}
```

This makes drift structurally impossible going forward -- one source of truth, not four independently-maintained copies. Import `detect_orchestrator` and `OrchestratorKind` in each adapter file if not already imported (check current imports first).

## Bug 2: boundary-truncated UTF-8 collapses the whole sample

`detect_orchestrator`'s first line: `let sample_str = std::str::from_utf8(sample_bytes).unwrap_or("");`. The function's own docstring says it reads "the first 2048 bytes of the log file header." If any multi-byte UTF-8 character (an emoji, an accented character in a real user prompt -- routine in real transcripts) straddles that 2048-byte boundary, `from_utf8` fails and `unwrap_or("")` discards ALL preceding valid bytes too, not just the broken tail -- a well-formed file becomes unrecognizable purely by chance of where the truncation boundary lands.

Fix: on a `Utf8Error`, recover the valid prefix via `Utf8Error::valid_up_to()` instead of discarding everything:

```rust
let sample_str = match std::str::from_utf8(sample_bytes) {
    Ok(s) => s,
    Err(e) => std::str::from_utf8(&sample_bytes[..e.valid_up_to()]).unwrap_or(""),
};
```

(the re-slice with `valid_up_to()` is guaranteed to succeed since that prefix is by definition valid UTF-8, but keep the `.unwrap_or("")` as a defensive fallback rather than a bare `.unwrap()`, consistent with this codebase's style).

## TDD steps

1. Write failing tests:
   - In crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs's existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: a test with a sample truncated mid-multi-byte-character (e.g. a valid ClaudeCode sample with sessionId+parentUuid markers, followed by a multi-byte UTF-8 character like 'café' or an emoji sliced at a byte offset that splits the character) asserting `detect_orchestrator` STILL correctly returns `Some(OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode)` (i.e. the valid prefix's markers are still found) rather than `None`.
   - In each of claude.rs/codex.rs/opencode.rs/agy.rs's own test modules (or add one if a file lacks inline tests -- check each file's current test coverage first): a parity test asserting `AdapterX.matches_fingerprint(sample) == (detect_orchestrator(sample.as_bytes()) == Some(OrchestratorKind::X))` across BOTH a matching sample and a genuinely non-matching sample, and specifically for ClaudeCodeAdapter, a test with `{"sessionId":"x","leafUuid":"y"}` (no parentUuid) asserting `matches_fingerprint` now correctly returns `false` (this is the concrete drift case -- confirm it's red against the current claude.rs before fixing).
2. Confirm red against current code (claude.rs's test should fail pre-fix; the UTF-8 truncation test should fail pre-fix).
3. Implement both fixes.
4. Confirm green: all new tests pass, full existing test suites for fingerprint.rs, test_claude.rs, test_codex.rs, test_opencode.rs, test_agy.rs all still pass with no regression.
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-session`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit both fixes together (one root-cause theme: fingerprint robustness/consistency) as one commit, or two commits if you judge they're cleanly separable -- your call, document which you chose and why.

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, and confirm the ClaudeCodeAdapter drift case is now fixed.

Read the current, exact `detect_orchestrator` function in crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs first. Then change ALL FOUR adapters' `matches_fingerprint` methods to delegate directly to `detect_orchestrator` instead of maintaining an independent boolean expression:

```rust
fn matches_fingerprint(&self, sample: &str) -> bool {
    detect_orchestrator(sample.as_bytes()) == Some(OrchestratorKind::ClaudeCode) // (or Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode as appropriate per adapter)
}
```

This makes drift structurally impossible going forward -- one source of truth, not four independently-maintained copies. Import `detect_orchestrator` and `OrchestratorKind` in each adapter file if not already imported (check current imports first).

## Bug 2: boundary-truncated UTF-8 collapses the whole sample

`detect_orchestrator`'s first line: `let sample_str = std::str::from_utf8(sample_bytes).unwrap_or("");`. The function's own docstring says it reads "the first 2048 bytes of the log file header."
```rust
let sample_str = match std::str::from_utf8(sample_bytes) {
    Ok(s) => s,
    Err(e) => std::str::from_utf8(&sample_bytes[..e.valid_up_to()]).unwrap_or(""),
};
```

2. Confirm red against current code (claude.rs's test should fail pre-fix; the UTF-8 truncation test should fail pre-fix).
3. Implement both fixes.
4. Confirm green: all new tests pass, full existing test suites for fingerprint.rs, test_claude.rs, test_codex.rs, test_opencode.rs, test_agy.rs all still pass with no regression.

input.prompt:
Execute via full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). Two related High-severity findings from an adversarial review, both in crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs's parse_stream. No plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from this brief.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: 6 fixes landed (cb29996..ba9de12), `cargo test --workspace` green.

## Bug 1: CRIT-LUMEN-163's explicit-null guard only checks top-level fields, but 3 of the 9 named fields are read from nested paths

Current code (crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/claude.rs, around line 84-104):
```rust
for field in ["id", "cwd", "model", "sessionId", "requestId", "version", "costUSD", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens"] {
    if val.get(field).map(|v| v.is_null()).unwrap_or(false) {
        parse_failures.push(ParseFailureRecord { session_id: session_id.clone(), line_number: idx + 1, byte_offset: 0, error: CompactString::new(format!("explicit null on field '{field}'")) });
        continue 'lines;
    }
}
```
This checks `val.get(field)` -- the JSONL entry's TOP LEVEL only. But the actual readers later in the same function read `model` from `message.model` (line ~145) and `cache_creation_input_tokens`/`cache_read_input_tokens` from `message.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`/`message.usage.cache_read_input_tokens` (lines ~156-157). An entry with `message.usage.cache_read_input_tokens: null` is NEVER caught by the current guard (it only checks the root, where that field doesn't exist at all), so `u.get("cache_read_input_tokens").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0)` later silently coerces the explicit null to 0 -- exactly the misparse this guard exists to prevent.

Fix: split the guard into (a) the 6 fields that genuinely live at the entry's top level -- id, cwd, sessionId, requestId, version, costUSD -- checked exactly as today, and (b) model/cache_creation_input_tokens/cache_read_input_tokens checked at their REAL nested locations: `message.model`, and `message.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`/`message.usage.cache_read_input_tokens` (only when a `message` object is present at all -- if there's no message object, there's nothing nested to check, that's a different, already-handled case). Use the same `continue 'lines` + ParseFailureRecord::push pattern for the nested checks, with a clear error message identifying the nested path (e.g. `"explicit null on field 'message.model'"`).

## Bug 2: byte_offset is hardcoded to the literal 0 in every ParseFailureRecord

Both `parse_failures.push(...)` call sites in parse_stream (the JSON-parse-error branch around line 67-72, and the null-guard branch(es)) hardcode `byte_offset: 0`. CRIT-LUMEN-025 requires a real byte offset. `reader.lines()` strips newlines and discards byte-position info, so track it manually: add `let mut byte_offset: usize = 0;` before the loop, and immediately after obtaining each line (before any other processing or `continue`), record `let line_start_offset = byte_offset;` then advance `byte_offset += line.len() + 1;` (the +1 approximates the stripped newline -- note in a code comment that this is an LF-based approximation and will undercount by 1 byte per line for CRLF-terminated input, which is an acceptable known limitation for a diagnostic field, not a byte-exact file-seek requirement). Use `line_start_offset` (the offset at the START of the line currently being processed) in place of the literal `0` in both existing ParseFailureRecord constructions, and in the new nested-null-check construction from Bug 1.

Read the CURRENT exact file content first (it may have shifted slightly from the excerpts above) before editing.

## TDD steps

1. Write failing tests in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_claude.rs (add to the existing file):
   - A line with `message.usage.cache_read_input_tokens: null` (nested null) -- assert the resulting transcript has a `parse_failures` entry recording it as malformed (not silently coerced to 0 cache_read_tokens), and that `economics`/turn-level cache_read is NOT incremented by that line.
   - A line with `message.model: null` (nested null) -- assert it's rejected via parse_failures, not silently leaving model_family at its hardcoded default with no signal.
   - Confirm the 6 genuinely-top-level fields (id, cwd, sessionId, requestId, version, costUSD) are STILL correctly rejected when null -- don't regress existing coverage (check the existing test for sessionId's null case still passes).
   - A test asserting `parse_failures[0].byte_offset` is a real, non-zero value for a malformed line that isn't the very first line in the file (construct a sample with at least one valid line before a malformed one, confirm byte_offset reflects real accumulated byte count, not 0). Also assert byte_offset for a malformed FIRST line is exactly 0 (correctly reflects the start of the file).
2. Confirm red against the current code (nested-null tests should fail since the guard doesn't check nested paths yet; byte_offset test should fail since it's hardcoded 0).
3. Implement both fixes.
4. Confirm green: new tests pass, full existing test_claude.rs suite passes with no regression (especially the existing corrupted-lines-resilience and explicit-null-sessionId tests).
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-session`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit both fixes together as one commit (same function, same parsing loop, one cohesive change).

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, and the exact nested-field-list you implemented.

Both `detect_orchestrator` and `CodexAdapter::matches_fingerprint` (crates/lumen-session/src/fingerprint.rs) accept `"type":"response_item"` as valid Codex content, alongside `"type":"event_msg"`. But `parse_stream`'s current logic (crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs, around line 82-88):
```rust
if val.get("type").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) != Some("event_msg") {
    continue;
}
let Some(payload) = val.get("payload") else { continue; };
match payload.get("type").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) { ... }
```
silently skips ANY line whose top-level `type` isn't exactly `"event_msg"` -- including `response_item` lines, with zero signal. A real Codex rollout file composed mostly of `response_item` lines gets correctly fingerprinted as Codex, then parsed into a transcript with zero turns and no indication anything was skipped.

## Important constraint: do NOT fabricate response_item's internal schema

There is no confirmed, real-data-verified schema for what a `response_item` payload actually contains internally (unlike `event_msg`'s `item_completed`/`token_count`/`thread_settings_applied` sub-types, which were verified against a real local Codex rollout file in earlier research this workspace has already done). Inventing parsing logic for fields you're guessing at would repeat the exact "confidently wrong format" mistake this whole review-and-fix effort exists to correct. Do NOT write speculative field-extraction logic for response_item's contents.

Make the currently-silent skip VISIBLE instead of inventing a parser for an unconfirmed format: when a line's top-level `type` is `"response_item"` specifically (not just any non-event_msg type), record a `ParseFailureRecord` noting it was recognized by fingerprint but is not yet implemented by this parser, then continue -- so the resulting transcript's `parse_failures` field proves something real was skipped, rather than silently reporting a "successful" empty-looking parse. Lines whose top-level `type` is something else entirely (neither `event_msg` nor `response_item`) should keep the current silent-skip behavior unchanged -- that's out of scope for this specific finding.

Restructure the dispatch as a match on `val.get("type").and_then(|v| v.as_str())` with three arms: `Some("event_msg")` (existing full payload-dispatch logic, unchanged), `Some("response_item")` (new: push a ParseFailureRecord with a clear message like `"response_item envelope recognized by fingerprint but not yet implemented by CodexAdapter::parse_stream"`, then continue), and the wildcard `_` (unchanged silent continue).

The one `parse_failures.push(...)` call site in the JSON-parse-error branch (around line 65-70) hardcodes `byte_offset: 0`. Read the CURRENT exact file content first before editing.

1. Write failing tests in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_codex.rs (add to the existing file):
   - A sample composed of one or more `{"type":"response_item", ...}` lines (any plausible envelope shape is fine since you're only testing that it's RECORDED, not that its contents are parsed) -- assert the resulting transcript has a non-empty `parse_failures` with an error message mentioning "response_item", and confirm `turns.len() == 0` is now accompanied by a real signal rather than looking like a clean empty session.

2. Confirm red against the current code.

4. Confirm green: new tests pass, full existing test_codex.rs suite passes with no regression.
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-session`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
6. Commit both fixes together as one commit.

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, and confirm you did NOT invent any response_item field-parsing logic.

input.description: Fix AGY model, call_id correlation, parse_failures
input.prompt:
Execute via full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). Three related High-severity findings in crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/agy.rs's parse_stream. No plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from this brief -- the design below is already worked out from reading the real code, follow it rather than re-deriving your own approach.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: 8 fixes landed (cb29996..f0826a4), `cargo test --workspace` green.

## Bug 1: model_family is permanently hardcoded to a false Claude model name

`let model_family = CompactString::new("claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022");` (line ~45) is set once and never reassigned anywhere in the file. Antigravity is a Gemini-lineage orchestrator, not Claude. Research this session (recorded in memory, already verified against real on-disk data) confirmed the real Antigravity transcript.jsonl schema's fields are: `step_index`, `source`, `type`, `status`, `created_at`, `content`, plus `thinking`/`tool_calls[]` on PLANNER_RESPONSE entries -- there is NO real model-name field anywhere in this confirmed schema. So there is no real signal to extract, and inventing a fake one would repeat the exact "confidently wrong format" mistake this review exists to correct.

Fix: change the hardcoded value from a SPECIFIC WRONG Claude model name to an honest, generic placeholder like `"antigravity-unknown-model"` (or similar -- your call on exact string, just make it clearly NOT a specific Claude/Gemini model name), with a code comment explaining AGY's real on-disk schema has no per-session model field (confirmed this session, not a TODO). This does not fix pricing accuracy on its own (an unrecognized model string still falls back to Sonnet's rate via PricingTable's existing CRIT-LUMEN-008 fallback, unchanged) -- the value of this fix is that the reported `model_family` field stops actively lying about being a specific Claude model, which matters for anyone reading/trusting that field downstream. Do not attempt to fix AGY's pricing accuracy in this task; that's a separate, larger problem requiring real Gemini pricing data this workspace doesn't have.

## Bug 2: tool-call and tool-result call_ids use two incompatible numbering schemes

Tool calls are minted as `format!("agy_call_{}", tool_calls.len())` (line ~119) -- a counter LOCAL to the current PLANNER_RESPONSE turn's tool_calls SmallVec, always restarting at 0 for each new turn. The following TOOL_RESULT constructs `format!("agy_call_{}", turns.len().saturating_sub(1))` (line ~144) -- a completely different number derived from the GLOBAL turns vector's length. These essentially never coincide, so no AGY tool call ever correlates to its result (this breaks the cross-turn correlation fix already landed in trajectory_dag.rs/pr_link.rs, commit 5a24852 -- those accumulators can only find a match if the call_id strings genuinely agree).

Fix: replace both ad-hoc numbering schemes with a real, internally-consistent correlation mechanism:
1. Add a persistent (not reset per-turn) monotonic counter, e.g. `let mut next_call_id: usize = 0;`, declared before the main parsing loop alongside `turns`/`started_at`/etc.
2. Add a `std::collections::VecDeque<CompactString>` FIFO queue, e.g. `let mut pending_call_ids: std::collections::VecDeque<CompactString> = std::collections::VecDeque::new();`, also declared before the loop.
3. When a tool_call is constructed (inside the PLANNER_RESPONSE branch's `for call in calls` loop): mint `let call_id = CompactString::new(format!("agy_call_{next_call_id}")); next_call_id += 1;`, use it for `CanonicalToolCall.call_id`, and ALSO push a clone of it onto `pending_call_ids.push_back(call_id.clone())`.
4. When a TOOL_RESULT is constructed: instead of the current `format!("agy_call_{}", turns.len().saturating_sub(1))`, pop the FRONT of the queue: `let call_id = pending_call_ids.pop_front().unwrap_or_else(|| CompactString::new(format!("agy_unmatched_result_{}", turns.len())));` -- this assumes calls and their results are processed in the same order they were issued (true for a single-threaded conversational transcript), and the fallback sentinel makes an unmatched result honestly identifiable rather than silently colliding with a real call_id.

## Bug 3: parse_failures is hardcoded empty despite silently discarding malformed lines

Line ~64: `Err(_) => continue,` on a JSON parse error, with zero record kept. The final `Ok(CanonicalTranscript { ..., parse_failures: SmallVec::new(), ... })` (line ~189) hardcodes it empty regardless. This is the exact same gap already fixed in claude.rs (commit 78f91cf) and codex.rs (commit f0826a4) -- mirror their established pattern exactly: enumerate lines (`reader.lines().enumerate()`, not the current plain `reader.lines()`), track a running `byte_offset: usize` counter with `line_start_offset` captured before advancing (same LF-approximation pattern, same documented limitation), push a real `ParseFailureRecord { session_id: session_id.clone(), line_number: idx + 1, byte_offset: line_start_offset, error: CompactString::new(e.to_string()) }` on parse error (capture the error `e` instead of discarding it with `Err(_)`), collect them into a `parse_failures: SmallVec<[ParseFailureRecord; 2]>` declared before the loop, and use that real vec instead of `SmallVec::new()` in the final struct literal.

Read the CURRENT exact file content first before editing -- this is a precise description of the real current logic, confirm line-for-line before changing anything.

## TDD steps

1. Write failing tests in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_agy.rs (add to the existing file):
   - `model_family` no longer equals the old hardcoded Claude string for a parsed session (assert it's NOT `"claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"` and, if you want a positive assertion too, that it equals whatever placeholder you chose).
   - A two-tool-call scenario (two PLANNER_RESPONSE turns each with one tool call, each followed by its own TOOL_RESULT turn) asserting the FIRST result's `tool_results[0].call_id` matches the FIRST call's `call_id`, and the SECOND result's matches the SECOND call's -- proving real correlation now works, not just that the strings look plausible. This is the concrete proof the cross-turn correlation accumulators (trajectory_dag/pr_link) will now actually find AGY's matches.
   - A malformed line in an otherwise-valid AGY sample produces a `parse_failures` entry with a real (non-hardcoded) `error` message and correct `line_number`, and a non-first malformed line has `byte_offset > 0`.
2. Confirm red against the current code (verify each new test genuinely fails pre-fix for the right reason -- e.g. the call_id-correlation test should fail because the current mismatched numbering produces non-matching call_ids).
3. Implement all three fixes.
4. Confirm green: new tests pass, full existing test_agy.rs suite passes with no regression (especially the existing double-json-parse and resolve-transcript-path tests, which are unrelated to these three bugs and should be untouched).
5. Run `cargo test -p lumen-session`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions -- pay particular attention to whether any lumen-analysis accumulator test (trajectory_dag/pr_link) that uses AGY fixtures now behaves differently now that call_ids actually correlate; that would be a GOOD sign the fix works end-to-end, not a regression, but confirm it doesn't break any existing assertion.
6. Commit all three fixes together as one commit (same file, same parsing loop, one cohesive "make AGY's adapter honest and internally consistent" change).

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, the exact placeholder model string you chose, and confirmation that the two-call correlation test proves real matching (not coincidental).
